expected_level_description: You can: - understand and help teams to apply a range of techniques to analyse data and provide insight - be proactive and present compelling findings that inform wider decisions - apply innovative approaches to resolve problems

You can: - choose the appropriate medium to communicate findings - shape and share communications relevant to the audience - present analysis and visualisations in clear ways to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, with support - give tactical recommendations based on your analysis and insight to inform decision making

You can: - participate in discussions determining which performance measurements are appropriate, with guidance from more experienced colleagues - demonstrate experience in turning business needs and goals into performance measures

skill: Quality assurance of data and analysis
expected_level_description: You can: - identify appropriate ways to collect, collate and prepare data - decide if data and analysis is accurate and fit for purpose - perform data preparation and cleansing with limited guidance - undertake quality assurance processes - peer-review colleagues’ outputs from data analysis to ensure quality
You can: - show an understanding of the core technical concepts related to the role, and can apply them

skill: Understanding analysis across the product life cycle
expected_level_description: You can: - understand how the needs of the team and product vary across the product life cycle - ensure the team is measuring performance as appropriate for the relevant service standard phase - manage the delivery of services or products at different phases - plan and look at data requirements in future phases

You can: - use quantitative and qualitative data about users to turn user focus into outcomes - deliver analysis and information that addresses stakeholder needs and provides recommendations - effectively collaborate with user researchers and other user-focused professions - guide others on approaches to understand user stories

You can: - identify, understand, communicate and work within constraints - challenge the validity of constraints - ensure that standards are being met - show an understanding of security and data privacy

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - run data quality checks and correct errors - explain data quality reports to colleagues
You can: - explain the difference between identifiable, pseudonymised, and anonymised data - follow the organisation's rules for suppressing small numbers in outputs
You can: - recognise and challenge behaviour that excludes others - consider different needs when you plan your work
